## Example 1.3 {#ss1-example-1-3}

For each sequence:

- Write down the next three terms
- Define the sequence by an $n$th term rule ($a_n$)

a) $1,4,7,10,\ldots$

b) $3,6,12,24,\ldots$

c) $1,4,9,16,\ldots$

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 2 · Example 1.3 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
Keep the source prompt unchanged. Explain verbally that we seek the intended simple patterns; a finite initial list does not uniquely determine an infinite continuation.

(a) 13,16,19; a_n=3n−2.
(b) 48,96,192; a_n=3×2^(n−1). Check n=1 to avoid an exponent of n.
(c) 25,36,49; a_n=n².

Ask students to test their proposed rule at n=1 and at a later displayed index. No general AP/GP formula is required yet.
:::
